answer: To deter Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens into a trust knoll, a focal bonding curve where each identity must forge an audit trail. Randomly selected multi-agent auditors sample communication graphs for sparse topological cuts. If clustered clones attempt collusion, audit proofs trigger automated stake slashing. Because discovering valid graph cuts across dense clusters requires superlinear attacker cost scaling with $O(N^2)$, honest verification blooms reliably like wild yarrow while dishonest replicas face swift ruin.
